newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 30.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 30.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Friday and main factors likely to affect trading:
* The Philippine equities market is likely to witness a pullback after six days of runup due to the slowdown in the first quarter GNP growth, traders said.
* "It will be the classic sell-on-news. Major blue chips that led the rallies will correct," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor-Hagedorn Securities.

* "With the GNP figures, analysts are thinking more on the negative side - that government will not meet its target for the year or at best GNP will remain unchanged from last year's," said Ramon Saulo, analyst at Asiamerit Securities.
* On Thursday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index closed 35.94 points higher at 2,758.61.
* The Dow Jones on Thursday ended 27.05 points lower to 7,330.18. PLDT's ADR dipped $0 3/4 to $57 3/8.

* The Philippines' first quarter GNP grew 6.1 percent against a revised 6.9 percent a year earlier, Planning Secretary Cielito Habito said. GDP rose 5.0 percent from a revised 5.1 percent in the same period last year.

* Habito said he is confident GNP growth this year would meet the government's 7-8 percent target. Economists, however, said that the Philippines is unlikely to meet the full-year optimistic growth targets.
* The National Economic and Development Authority said it expects inflation to slow down further in May from 4.6 percent in April.

* Three U.S. legislators urged Manila to fulfill its promise to the World Trade Organisation on fair market access for pork. U.S. meat producers have complained to the trade body that the Philippines blocked fair market access for U.S. pork.
* The Securities and Exchange Commission told the stock exchange to develop a system that will immediately determine the level of foreign ownership in companies.
* Standard & Poor's Corp said it had placed the AA-minus/A1-plus ratings of Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd and the AA-minus rating of subsidiary Coca-Cola Amatil (NZ) Ltd on negative credit watch.
* Asia Amalgamated Holdings Corp said it posted a net income of 8.36 million pesos in 1996 from a 6.76 million net loss the previous year.
* Cosmos Bottling Corp, the beverage arm of RFM Corp, said it expects to post a net income of 476.94 million pesos in 1997.
* Philippine crude imports rose 2.2 percent to 32.41 million barrels in the first quarter of the year against 31.70 million in the same period last year, the energy department said.

* Newspaper Manila Bulletin reported that the deficit of the Oil Price Stabilisation Fund rose by 158 million pesos to 2.56 billion pesos as of May 14 due to the fluctuations in the peso-dollar foreign exchange rate.
The buffer fund was abolished after the full deregulation of the oil inddustry in February but government has yet to settle the amount it owes the oil firms.
* The Central Bank had cut its overnight borrowing and lending rates by two percentage points each on Thursday. It also lowered its term reverse repo rates following the two-percentage point cut.
* The Philippine peso closed lower at 26.374 to the dollar vs 26.372.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average slipped to 16.03125 percent from 18.03125.
